background: Bendigo and Adelaide Bank is Australia's largest regional bank, funded mainly by retail deposits raised through a community-branch model and lending mainly on residential mortgages and to farms and small businesses.
synthesis: Rated A- on average across all three, all three on a stable outlook, after a one-notch upgrade by one of the three on 21 Nov 2025, the lowest rating among the Australian banks a depositor is likely to consider. Capital is the weak spot, with CET1 of 11.3% in the bottom quarter of Australian banks. Liquidity is the strength, LCR of 140% in the top quarter and NSFR of 115% above the median. None of the ratios has moved materially over the past four periods to 30 Jun 2026.
